question: Some important administrative posts were hereditary during the Rashtrakuta and Chola dynasties. What the post ‘nagara-shreshthi’ meant?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Merchant of the city**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Rashtrakuta dynasty, the **King **was the head of administration and the** Commander-in-Chief** of the armed forces.
 
• Some **posts were made hereditary**, which meant that the son got a particular post after the death of his father.
 
• For example, Poet **Harisena **was a **Maha-danda-nayaka** (Chief Judicial Officer) and his father held the same post.
 
• **Nagara-Shreshti** was the term used for the **top banker or merchant of the city**. Prashasti: It is a Sanskrit word which means 'in praise of. The court poets used to praise their rulers in glowing terms.
 
• These policies appear quite effective in keeping control over the kingdom to a certain extent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administration Of Chola Kingdom**

 
 
• The Central Government, Provincial Government, and Local Government were the three main administrative tiers under the Cholas.
 
• The names of the higher-ranking authorities were **Peruntaram **and the lower-ranking officials were Siruntaram.
 
• The Chola Empire was split into nine provinces, each with its own administration. Another name for them was **Mandalams**.
 
• **Viceroy **was the title given to the province's leader. Viceroys were chosen from the monarchs' close family members
 
• **Nattars **were the name given to the nadus' heads. The Nattavai was the name of the nadu council.
 
• Agriculture was pushed by Nattavais and Nattar representatives. In addition, they were in charge of tax collection and population protection.
 
• **Variyams **assisted Local Assemblies in carrying out village government efficiently. These variyams were made up of male members of the community.
